behavior: A press of the trigger can open the popup of `Menu` or `Select`. An item does not activate when the release of that press comes within 8 px of the point of the press on each axis. The open can put an item under a pointer that does not move: a layout change can move the trigger, and `alignItemWithTrigger` puts the selected item of `Select`, or its first item, under the pointer. Base UI activates that item when the release comes 200 ms or more after the press (`Menu`), or 400 ms or more after the open (`Select`): the menu runs the action of the item, and the select commits the value of the item. The rule applies in each mode of `Select`, also when the popup aligns the selected item with the trigger. A native pop-up button of macOS commits the selected item and closes for a release with no move after a hold. Vase UI keeps the popup open, so one gesture has one result in each mode and for each duration of the press. `Context Menu` opens at the point of a right press. An item of a context menu does not activate when the release comes within 8 px of that point on each axis. By default, the popup starts 2 px right of that point and 5 px above it, so its first item can start a few pixels from the pointer. Base UI ignores only a release within 1 px of that point, at any time after the open. With that rule, a right click on macOS that moves 3 px onto the first item of the demo on the Context Menu page runs the action of that item. On other platforms, an item ignores the release of the right button. A move of 8 px or less on each axis is not a drag. `Select.Item` of Base UI takes 8 px of vertical travel as the start of a drag across its items. 8 px is less than half of the 24 px target of WCAG 2.2. A hand that moves 8 px or less on each axis during a long press thus activates no item. A release more than 8 px from the point of the press on one axis still activates the item under it.
